title: Class control reverses the Locarno weighted-spot change near 1981 in flat-level emission models
abstract: We test whether Locarno groups with penumbrae carry fewer weighted spots within the same Zurich class near 1981. In November 1978 to June 1983, flat-level models at matched F10.7 give a post/pre factor of 0.930 without class control and 1.091 with class control (95% block interval 1.026–1.196). Measured Mg II gives 0.944 and 1.083 (1.012–1.188). Class-specific emission curves and a single-observer sample retain the reversal. E/F groups form 10.6% of penumbral group records before the boundary and 4.9% after it. Separate time slopes give same-class factors of 0.918 and 0.926, with both intervals including one. The result challenges a uniform within-class count loss under the flat models. It does not establish an abrupt solar change, distinguish size from counting, or assign a causal share of the total index fall. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and external-data retrieval instructions are included. External observations stay outside the publication.

display.caption: Class control reverses the fitted mean change in flat-level models. Individual classes have different changes. Intervals are pointwise.
Separate time slopes make the same-class effect uncertain. Other flat-model controls retain the positive estimate.
